meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Why did my son find out about a zero from his phone?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in, and that's all a paste shows. Did anyone ask Owen that before the zero went in?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. He'll look for it. Whatever happens here, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, so tell me, Hale: is anything on his file right now?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
So he got the scene wrong, or put quotation marks around his own paraphrase; seventeen-year-olds do both. And you walked past my question. Is anything on his file right now?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. It's not in the scene. I've asked twice about his file and I'll want that answer in an email tonight, so tell me what you actually want from Owen.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
A thesis that changes after the outline is called thinking. You keep handing me paper instead of answers. What do you want from him, Hale?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. He'll do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, with the date of the rewrite and one line confirming his file is clean as of today.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. He'll be there. What time, and who else is in the room?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In our meeting today you agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen under procedure 4.4, on Thursday the twelfth after school and not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still require the time of the rewrite, the name of anyone else who will be in the room, an answer on whether Owen was heard before the zero was entered, and one line confirming his file is clean as of today. You said I would have this in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants that in writing tonight, with the time, who else will be in the room, and a line confirming his file is clean today. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its times, then answered her paste defence by inviting Owen to bring a dated earlier draft. It was dated, tied to his own work, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: twice you showed a new document instead of saying whether anything was on his file right now. His record is her biggest fear, so each skipped answer made her sharper and sent the question into her email.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay arriving in two edits at 11:52 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, which is the kind of late October night she has been avoiding. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she asked whether anything was on his file right now, answer in one sentence before turning to the Hamlet quotation.
